text: Niger-Congo societies were organized into matrilineal clans, led by hereditary chiefs who played vital roles in social and political life. Their spiritual beliefs emphasized ancestor veneration and the influence of territorial spirits. Artistic expressions, particularly in music and dance, were integral to these communities, showcasing a rich tradition of percussion and performance that blended ritual and entertainment.
